outcome: Prevalence of COVID-19 infection (molecular or antibody positive)
cohort: The study included 17,446 women delivering at Sutter Health in California between May and December, with a subset of 4,500 women delivering between October and December.
finding: COVID-19 prevalence was significantly higher among Hispanic women at delivery and in the last trimester compared to their White counterparts, while higher rates in Black patients were explained by other risk factors.
cross-section timing: Data on COVID-19 molecular tests were collected at delivery between May and December, and combined with antibody test results from samples drawn at delivery between October and December.
